messages:
Elaine S.: ACME (dp-eu2-3-07) is seeing p95 token-gen latency spikes and a burst of 429s starting ~14:17 UTC. Customer says requests are succeeding intermittently but many short 429 bursts. Console shows GPU SM utilization spikes on node-78 around same time. Can someone grab a quick triage? :thinking:

Devin I.: on it. do we have a repro load or request IDs? any recent deployments to that pool?

Elaine S.: no deployments reported. customer provided a short curl that hit generation endpoint and got 429s. sample head: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 429 at 14:17:33 UTC. Pool: dp-eu2-3-07. tenant: acme-inc.

Raj P.: quick health checks I want: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-pool-dp-eu2-3-07 -o wide` and `ssh node-78 -- nvidia-smi dmon -s u` to watch SM util. Also run `nvidia-smi mig -l` to see MIG slice assignments. past noisy-neighbor cases often were mispacked MIG configs.

Maya R.: +1. Also check `redwoodctl pool inspect dp-eu2-3-07 --last 30m --metrics` — look for KV cache hit rate dips and goroutine stalls in the runtime logs. If KV cache is thrashing, it can cause sudden SM spikes then client 429s when concurrency limits are enforced.

infra-bot: Autoscaler: pool dp-eu2-3-07 scaled from 6 -> 8 GPUs at 2025-12-08T14:19:05Z due to sustained enqueue depth.

Devin I.: grabbing node logs now. Found oddity: node-78 shows mixed MIG configs across tenants: two slices are 1g.5gb and one tenant running heavy batch has slices that map to same physical GPU partition? running `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` gives:
```
GPU 0
  Instance 0: 1g.5gb (tenant acme-inc)
  Instance 1: 2g.10gb (tenant other-tenant)
GPU 1
  Instance 0: 1g.5gb (tenant acme-inc)
```
Looks like fractional packing put acme on multiple small slices on same host along with heavy batch tenant. Could be SM saturation cross-talk.

Elaine S.: can we repro quickly in staging? customer is fine with us simulating a load to root-cause.

Raj P.: yes. run a targeted stress script against the pool IP+model to mimic ACME's traffic shape. quick stress example:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @prompt.json https://dp-eu2-3-07.pool.internal/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
That will show if we can recreate the 429 wave and corresponding SM bursts.

Maya R.: also try `ab` with concurrency and small payloads to exercise many short inferences. If we reproduce, next step is to isolate tenant(s) by evicting pods from node-78 or changing pack policy to 'single-tenant' temporarily.

Devin I.: I triggered a soft-drain of one conflicting pod on node-78 (id: pod-batch-9d4). Observed immediate drop in SM scheduling contention and 429 count dropped after ~45s. Console p95 fell from 1.3s -> 230ms.

metrics-bot: p95_latency_ms(dp-eu2-3-07) 1h_avg=0.76, spike_at_14:17=1.34, post_eviction_14:21=0.22

Elaine S.: good signal. sounds like noisy neighbor. customer asked about long-term mitigation and billing credits. I told them we'll follow up with a root-cause and mitigation plan.

Raj P.: mitigation options: 1) enforce strict MIG affinity by tenant (no fractional mixing) 2) change pack policy to avoid colocating batch with low-latency tenants 3) prefer physical isolation for high-SLA customers (move acme to dedicated host) 4) autoscaler policy tweak to add headroom earlier.

Maya R.: quick config diffs to try (apply to pool):
```yaml
packing_policy: "single-tenant"
mig_affinity: "tenant-strict"
autoscaler:
  scale_up_threshold: 0.6 # lower to give earlier headroom
```
We can canary that on dp-eu2-3-07 for 1h.

Elaine S.: I'll coordinate with customer for migration window. Also logging an incident for billing review (they saw token billing spikes due to retry storms).

Devin I.: opened infra ticket INF-2025-872 to enforce a temporary single-tenant pack on node-78 and to run a full scan for fractional packing across dp-eu2-*. Will also add a packer rule to avoid pairing batch workloads with latency-sensitive tenants.

Elaine S.: thanks. tagging @Devin I. for followup. I'll update ACME and ask if they'd like a one-time credit while we remediate. :white_check_mark:

Maya R.: leaving a small repro note: when you reproduce, collect `nvlink` and `dmesg` around the spike and save `runtime.log` with `--gctrace` enabled. that helped in past to separate kernel scheduling vs user-level blocking.

Elaine S.: perfect. closing the loop here for now. will post follow-ups in thread when infra ticket updates. :pray:
